newsitem.title: USA: Knape & Vogt Modar unit offer withdrawn.
newsitem.headline: Knape & Vogt Modar unit offer withdrawn.

text.p: Knape & Vogt Manufacturing Co said Wednesday Fournier Furniture Inc has withdrawn its offer to buy the firm's Modar unit.
"Due to a number of factors they determined it wasn't a good fit for them," said Knape & Vogt spokesman Rick Simkins.
Knape & Vogt continues to talk to two interested parties, Simkins said. If no buyer is found by March 31, 1997, Modar will be liquidated, he said.

Fournier, of St. Paul, Va., announced on October 24 that it would purchase Modar for an undisclosed price. Based in Benton Harbor, Mich, Modar makes free-standing wood shelving. It continues to operate at a reduced level with 60 to 65 workers.
Knape & Vogt said in June it would sell or liquidate Modar as part of a restructuring.

"Although we do not anticipate a significant material impact, there may be additional costs incurred in concluding an eventual sale or phasing out of the operation," Allan Perry, Knape & Vogt president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The purchase price from Fournier was consistent with the loss reserve set by Knape & Vogt at the time of its restructuring, it said.

The company said its 1994 acquisition of its Hirsch unit made the Modar operation redundant. Modar workers will be laid off unless they can be found other jobs within Knape & Vogt, Simkins said. Knape & Vogt makes wall-attached and free- standing shelving, storage products and other home furnishing items.
